P0, church access / FIXES 6/20: church-entry-a-c6 is pasted across the church's window/buttress at x672–768,y912–960. This does not establish a coherent east-facing ground entrance. See critic-r17C6-1-floating-church-entry-4x.png.

P0, enclosure / FIXES 1/2 and coordinator: the northwest, northeast and southern groups still read as narrow building islands on continuous cobbles. Examples are the broad rear apron x864–1056,y288–528, the open northeast slots around x1584–1680,y288–480, and the southern frontage groups separated by broad undifferentiated paving. A positive-length ground contact with any one neighbour/store is insufficient evidence of closed property strips or continuous street frontage. The new north/south rear assemblies also overlap vertically instead of providing legible enclosed blocks.

P0, compulsory street variation / FIXES 2: the five north-wall-lane rectangles merge into one unchanged 1728x48 strip, x96–1824,y240–288. Dividing it into records of at most 384 px has not introduced an actual frontage jog, bend or width change. The northwest elbow and 48 px southern stagger are real improvements, but the long-run rule is not met everywhere.

P0, volume / FIXES 3/4 and panel 2 house approval: the complete merchant-house comparison still has a tall rectangular roof over a flat panel stack. The 12 px masonry strip reads as a front pilaster, not a receding shaded end connected to eave and plinth. In the five-/one-storey proofs the coping starts below the eave and the lower roof merely butts against that stripe. Thick repeated floor belts and unrelated bay arrangements remain conspicuous in west-0 and merchant-3. The house does not yet read as the reference house's architectural neighbour.

P0, roof assembly / FIXES 4/10/13: x1488–1584,y240–432 shows successive caps restarting in the same vertical roof column, including a straight transverse restart around y288. At x1632–1776,y480–624 the side-house/flat cap/narrow roof overlap without a convincing valley or height transition. Side-house roofs also hide earlier houses' lower facades. Close contacts using roof and wall geometry for the actual footprint and height, rather than overlapping whole painted rectangles.

P0, material scale / FIXES 10: the old hip beside the guildhall at x720–816,y336–480 and its slate partner at x1104–1200,y288–432 still switch from broken fine dashes on the slope to a large straight brick grid on the end triangle. New merchant caps and large-tile side houses introduce still other scales. The six abutment-b exports do not supply compatible courses. The whole roof family has not been unified.

P0, civic hierarchy / FIXES 5: the guildhall has moved to base y720 and its immediate infill flanks are lower, but its occupied body is still a small ornate insertion below the neighbouring merchant roof masses. At 1x greyscale the clock is recognizable while the arcade/body remains subordinate to the surrounding window stacks. The requested broad dominant civic mass and quieter neighbours are not visibly achieved.

P0, shadows / FIXES 11: the north curtain's shadow restarts with a lit triangular notch at each panel boundary, for example x480/576/672,y240–264. Attached frontage shadows likewise stop at the lot's right edge and restart rather than continuing through a shared contact. c6_render projects each bottom 48 px caster row into a width-clipped apron, then subtracts all occupied architecture; it supplies no separate receiving-wall/roof projection. Opacity 88/255 and angular edges pass, but the structural continuity requirement does not. See critic-r17C6-1-wall-shadow-resets-4x.png.

P0, tower integration / FIXES 9/13: the open and bell tower composites have exposed cut-and-paste shaft transitions, repeated across the city. Matching curtain A/B/C edge columns does not establish compatibility with these towers or the darker stair return. See the two failed tower PNG entries.

notes: Independent harsh saved-art critic, C6 round 1. The final critic-only instruction controls: no production art, composer, notes, branches, commits or pushes were changed. Only this JSON and critic-r17C6-1-*.png review composites were written. Read BRIEF-17 in full, both panel briefs, all twenty C6 fixes and the five underlying reviews, the Part E critic and NOTES method sections. BRIEF-17 takes precedence over panel waivers for fixed rows, 1–2-cell building depth, twice-R15 sign scale, lot-contained overlays, compulsory street variation and civic/gate allocations; the coordinator's 40x30 cells sets 1920x1440 rather than the earlier approximate 1200x900. Inspected all 66 C6 exports at exact native scale and nearest-neighbour 4x, their colour partners, the complete city at 1x and sixteen 4x crops covering it, its squint, native reference houses/halls, the complete-house 1x/4x proof, both tall/low hands, wall/stair contacts, roof/abutment variant sheets and actor normal/reveal proofs. The 2x and all three 3x deliveries are pixel-exact rescalings of the inspected final; the comparison is exact over its opaque backing. Inspected all nine reused ground bases in literal 3x3 repeats at 1x/4x, and life props over summer grass, city cobbles and courtyard ground. There are no seasonal partners in C6, so seasonal-ground/seasonal-silhouette tests are not applicable; all sixteen slate/brown alpha masks match their terracotta source exactly. All 66 exports match inventory dimensions, have alpha only 0/255, zero RGB under transparency and no detached one/two-pixel alpha components. All ten checked C6 ground/upper/inn stack modules preserve course rows 0/47. Curtain A-B/B-C/C-A first/last two columns match. Retained image-tool prompts, mode-sampling records and native compositing operations were reviewed; this review did not generate replacement art or replay every recorded mode sample. Imported compose.py with bytecode disabled; a fresh in-memory C6 render exactly matches the saved final. Independently recounted 49 modular buildings: storeys 1:4, 2:24, 3:12, 4:6, 5:3. The supplied ancillary-inclusive accounting is 59 buildings, 1:13, 2:25, 3:12, 4:6, 5:3 (22.03% one-storey), below 25%. Roof-family count independently confirmed: 22 terracotta, 19 slate, 8 brown; mixed roofs are preserved. No frontage lawn was found. The square is 480x336 (10x7 cells) with a 96x96 notch; six stalls and the gate road are present. Independently hashed the saved forty consecutive-house windows: no facade/roof count violation in those windows. Part E L-block/market/height audits pass (28/21/16 windows). The broader existing audit FAILS the churchyard fence chain, as recorded above. The frontend/runtime was not exercised and no collision/pathfinding approval is claimed. Fix-by-fix disposition: 1 incomplete enclosure; 2 main gate route improved but long unchanged wall lane/enclosure still fail; 3 house-depth approval fails; 4 contacts/occlusion incomplete; 5 required move and lower flanks done but civic mass still fails; 6 north arcade provided but east church steps fail integration; 7 named shop openings/landings and inn porch/bed cue provided; 8 pump court, open passage and reveal provided, subject to the surrounding assembly failures; 9 curtain edge contract repaired but tower/stair assembly incomplete; 10 family texture scale incomplete; 11 opacity/angularity improved but structural joins fail; 12 original facade repeat repaired but global repetition still fails on fences; 13 alternate side-house art and southern stagger provided, with roof/tower integration still failing; 14 new symbols readable as files but scribe hidden in final; 15 six stalls/two rows and eastern route retained; 16 working gate landing fails; 17 fuel/store provided but yard-alpha compositing fails; 18 shrine/pump visible but forge smoke invisible; 19 varied vendors and paired shoppers provided but cart replacement duplicates the old placement; 20 proofs exist and technical scales pass, but visible blockers remain. A pass on an isolated PNG does not approve its placement. The nine failed asset entries identify drawing/asset-assembly faults; the other visible failures are assigned to compose.py and its seven final render products.
